blocks.text: “Nature is my imaginary playground where the impossible becomes possible.”

In the Phantasma series, my visual language moves toward imagination, dreams, and fantasy. Guided by a singular creative vision since 1998, my artistic work delves into the intricate relationships between memory, the past, and nature. Through my work, I delve into the subconscious, childhood, alternative and potential narratives, shared collective emotions, associations, and the inner self.

My creative process always begins with the search for a place that inspires me; the landscape itself invites me to build unique, site-specific fabric installations, which I then photograph. I am deeply drawn to uninhabited, secluded environments that hold no economic value. For me, the significance of nature lies in the human capacity to see it as a source of creation and imagination.

This time, my journey has led me to the silent, untamed landscapes of Lapland and Iceland, where nature strips away the unnecessary, leaving only the essential: stone, ice, wind, and light. To me, this barrenness is not empty—it is a space of extreme beauty and a canvas for the subconscious. These places work as psychological mindscapes, site-specific mise-en-scènes, and metaphors for the human mind, childhood memories, and internal psychology. By focusing on these fragile, untouched territories, my work serves as a silent advocacy for nature—a poetic plea to respect and protect the untamed world.

The Phantasma series builds upon my long-standing photographic practice of working with landscape, place, second-hand clothing, ribbons and fabrics. Within the scenery, the garments form shapes resembling human figures, spirits, or ghosts—creating a poignant, imaginary meeting and a dialogue between the viewer, the landscape, and the invisible. A mere fabric in the scenery is only a starting point. Through this process, an everyday landscape can be perceived in an entirely new way. By precisely framing the landscape, choosing the perfect light and atmosphere, and sculpting the fabric, I seek a balance and interaction between the material and the place.

Operating entirely as a one-woman project, I always work alone in the silence of the wilderness. Being alone enables me to face my inner self, focus on the essential, and allow my imagination to expand. This solitary process sets clear boundaries for my work, forcing me to rely entirely on my intuition and strength. Working on nature’s terms means adapting to the unpredictable—navigating sudden shifts in weather, wind, and light, which actively shape the outcome of each work. In these intense moments, I carry out every step of this slow process, capturing these fleeting encounters on 4×5-inch film with a large format field camera.

I am especially interested in shared collective emotions and how to convey profound, wordless feelings through artistic means. I seek a layer of existence and emotion that is not physically present but awakened in the viewer’s mind, shaped by their personal history and experiences. For me, the emotional resonance conveyed by the final image is always as vital—maybe even more so—than the physical subject matter within the frame.

Among the ancient rocks, The Guardian of Water emerged—whispering that even in the most rugged terrain, there is a hidden, protective grace. Phantasma invites one to see beyond the visible, where the harshness of nature meets the softness of a dream.
Selected Awards & Prizes: • 2020 – LensCulture Exposure Awards, Finalist and Juror’s Pick • 2011 – William Thuring Prize, The Fine Arts Society of Finland
